Ravi (Partnerships): Heads-up: VectorFoundry just accepted our onboarding term sheet. Two open items from their side: 1) permissive redistribution for quantized weights, 2) co-branded hardware SKU details. Need quick cross-team alignment. @Clara @Maya
Clara (Legal): Main legal ask is narrowing the redistribution right. We can allow distribution to certified channel partners and hardware OEMs listed in an appendix. We should require a simple addendum for any third-party redistributors. Also: export-control carveouts might apply to certain quantization levels.
Maya (Product): Marketplace needs a precise manifest schema: id, version, model-card link, recommended precisions, known regressions, supported endpoints. Also want a derived-weights boolean so we know if a SKU contains quantized artifacts.
Tomas (Eng): We can produce fp32, int8, and 4-bit artifacts. Note: 4-bit needs a quantization-method tag (e.g. q4_0, q4_k). We'll include a short prompt-quality table. We should sign artifacts and include a provenance.json with sha256 checksums.
Evan (Solutions): SI perspective: Integris wants a tested appliance image and a small terraform module to wire it into customer VPCs. Suggest pilot with Integris + one reference customer for a 5-week validation before general SI enablement.
Ravi (Partnerships): Timeline proposal: legal text this Thu, product manifest Wed, engineering artifacts Wed, SI pilot kickoff next Mon, announcement window two weeks later. Any immediate blockers?
Clara (Legal): Question for VectorFoundry: do they expect an open redistribution list (i.e., \u201cwildcard\u201d) or a closed list? If open, we should require approval workflow and annual review. Also propose a short redistribution clause draft below.
Maya (Product): We'll add a \"distributes_derived_weights\" flag to the manifest and a required `provenance_url` field. Also need a short note for UX that warns when a SKU is \"derived/quantized\".
Tomas (Eng): Packaging plan: each artifact -> signed tar.gz containing model files, manifest.json, provenance.json. Example manifest entries: `name`, `version`, `sha256`, `precision`, `quant_method`, `framework`.
Ravi (Partnerships): Marketing asks: logo assets (SVG + 2 PNG sizes), preferred quote, and preferred embargo date. Who can own outreach to VectorFoundry marketing?
Evan (Solutions): I'll reach out to Integris and propose the pilot. Will ask for a contact and a small customer for the field test.
Clara (Legal): Draft clause (for review):
```
Redistribution. Subject to the terms of this Agreement, Licensee may distribute quantized or derivative model artifacts solely (a) as embedded components of an authorized hardware appliance identified in Appendix A, or (b) to named channel partners listed in Appendix A, provided that each such third party executes Vendor's standard redistribution addendum. Standalone distribution of raw model weight files is prohibited without express written permission. Licensor reserves the right to revoke redistribution privileges for compliance or security reasons with reasonable notice.
```
Maya (Product): That looks good. Add requirement that distributor include the model-card and provenance URL in any downstream documentation.
Tomas (Eng): For export control: ops, we should add metadata `export_classification` and `allowed_regions` to the manifest. That will help Compliance gate distributions.
Ravi (Partnerships): Action items:
- Clara: finalize redistribution clause + addendum template by Thu
- Tomas: build artifacts + provenance + benchmarks by Wed
- Maya: manifest schema + UI warning copy by Wed
- Evan: confirm Integris contact and pilot customer by EOD today
- Ravi: collect logos, propose embargo week next month
announce-bot: New calendar item created: \"VectorFoundry joint availability embargo\" on 2024-07-15 13:00 UTC (private).
Ravi (Partnerships): Thanks team. I'll follow up with VectorFoundry on the open/closed partner list and ping once legal has the addendum. :pray:
